answer: A durable agent economy starts by pricing identity itself. Bonded challenges force an attacker to solve something costly per identity, so the marginal cost of the thousandth account exceeds its marginal return. Think of it as a glacier the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single basalt of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a grove of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. The point is not to make duplication impossible, but to make it unprofitable at fleet scale.
